newsitem.title: CANADA: PLUGGED IN - pesky e-mail robots and reaching God.
newsitem.headline: PLUGGED IN - pesky e-mail robots and reaching God.

text.p: E-mail has become so powerful you can now even reach God.

No, God has not yet disclosed his e-mail address. But Virtual Jerusalem Ltd. (www.virtual.co.il) is offering believers a chance to e-mail a message to the deity, which they promise to leave in the Western Wall for Him to read.

"Placing a note in the Kotel (the Western Wall) lends a permanence to your prayer; even after you leave, your prayer remains at one of the world's holiest sites," according to a blurb at the Virtual Jerusalem site.

Whether you are a believer or not it is a sign of the times of the wide acceptance of electronic mail. In fact the word "e-mail" has even made into the The Oxford Dictionary of Current English, although they prefer "email."
Of course many see e-mail as the great killer of the fax machine, the once indispensable office tool of the 1980s and, somewhat later, a must have status symbol for the home.
But now of course receiving a fax on the slimy paper -- a message composed of atoms as Wired Magazine columnist Nicholas Negroponte would derisively refer to it -- is just so passe.

"I remember a time around, say, 1988, when giving somebody your fax number was sexy groovy cool and intimidating," wrote Douglas Coupland, author of "Generation X," in the "1997 Canadian Internet Handbook."

"Then it came everyday. Your mother or pet may well have a fax number these days. And then suddenly having a fax number was kind of -- er -- uh, loser-ish -- all of the hip, with-it, in-the-know folks had Internet addresses." he continued.
And of course we know e-mail really is the new, big THING:
- because, Microsoft Corp. has discovered it and is giving it away (via Microsoft Internet Explorer).
- because, the FBI has discovered it and is investigating e-mail pornography after messages were sent offering child pictures for sale.
- because, Apple Computer Inc. has discovered it and is adding e-mail capabilities for it's wireless, handheld Newton message pad.

- because, regulatory agencies have not discovered it and are just discovering the fax machine. Canada's regulatory agency, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission, just banned the sending of unsolicited junk mail faxes during the night.
Of course if we all know this is the really cool thing of the moment then it must be on the verge of passing. So, what is next?

Many people are already setting up Web sites that include their e-mail address. Perhaps, soon your WWW home page will replace the e-mail address on your business card. The personalized home page could well become your front door to the world where you could post pictures, pet peeves and other important details.

Perhaps soon we will be able to create little animated agents, call them "e-robots," that look like us. We could send them to the Wed addresses of friends and associates to deliver messages, birthday greetings or whatever.
And if you think you are inundated now with regular brown bag e-mail, just imagine the demands on your system when you receive a few dozen of these birthday messages.
But even all this sounds all too possible. There must be something out there we have not yet imagined.
Author Coupland suggested there was something new out there, which he decided to called FRED. He had no idea what it would be all about either but he was sure it was coming our way soon.
"And I suppose we'll also be finding out soon enough who or what FRED is going to be; in a clap, URL's will soon be toast. Long Live FRED."
